issues.title: `gh auth status --no-refresh` shows a misleading error for expired tokens

story.gist: With `--no-refresh`, `gh auth status` now reports an expired expiring token as "has expired". It shows the expiry lines and says to rerun without `--no-refresh`. If the refresh token has also expired, it suggests `gh auth login`.
story.goal: Make `gh auth status --no-refresh` explain an expired expiring token instead of calling it invalid and suggesting `gh auth refresh`.
story.why: With `--no-refresh`, an expired expiring token gets a 401 and is reported as invalid. The hint then points to the interactive `gh auth refresh`, though dropping the flag would renew the token (issue 14814).

changes.before: "Failed to log in… token is invalid"
Expiry details hidden on this failure
changes.after: Token and refresh-token expiry lines shown

changes.before: Refresh token also expired: still `gh auth refresh`
Expiry lines written inline for success

scenarios.title: Expired token checked with --no-refresh
scenarios.trigger: User runs `gh auth status --no-refresh` after the access token expired

steps.what: The `--no-refresh` option is now passed down to the entry builder.
The stale token is sent unchanged to the scope check.
The API answers HTTP 401 Bad credentials.
If the flag is set, the token is expiring, the error is 401 and expiry has passed, the entry is flagged.
The error branch sees the flag and prints the expired message instead of the generic one.
Token and refresh token expiry lines are printed.
If the refresh token is also past expiry, it suggests `gh auth login`. Otherwise it says to rerun without `--no-refresh`.

scenarios.title: Revoked or unreachable token with --no-refresh
scenarios.trigger: Token is rejected but not expired, or the API returns 503

steps.what: The scope check runs as before.
The API returns 401 with an unexpired token, or a non-401 error such as 503.
The condition fails, so the flag stays false.
The old "Failed to log in… invalid" output is printed.

stops.title: Detect the expired token
stops.summary: After a failed scope check, the entry builder flags the case where a 401 hit an expiring token past its expiry time.
stops.purpose: This decides which message is shown. Without it, the expired token still looks like any other rejected token.

necessity.reason: This is the detection logic; without it nothing distinguishes an expired token from a revoked one.

points.text: A new display-only field records that the token expired and no refresh was allowed.
points.why: so the renderer can choose the message without changing the JSON output.

points.text: The error is unwrapped to an HTTP error to read its status code.
points.why: so only a real 401 is treated as an expiry symptom.

points.text: The flag needs `--no-refresh`, an expiring token, a 401 and an expiry time not after now.
points.why: so revoked tokens, 503s and clock-skew successes keep their current behaviour.

stops.check: Confirm `entry.Refreshable` and `TokenExpiresAt` are already set before this early return, and that `errors.AsType` exists in the Go version used.

stops.title: Pass the no-refresh option down
stops.summary: The `--no-refresh` option is added to the entry builder's options and set at both call sites.
stops.purpose: The detection only applies when refresh was skipped. Without the flag, `buildEntry` cannot tell why the token was stale.

necessity.reason: `buildEntry` has no other way to know `--no-refresh` was set.

points.text: A new `noRefresh` field is added to the options struct.
points.why: so the builder can condition detection on the option.

points.text: The active account call site passes the option through.
points.why: so the active account gets the new message.

points.text: The other-accounts loop passes it too.
points.why: so inactive accounts behave the same as the active one.

stops.check: Check that every `buildEntry` call site sets `noRefresh`; the diff shows two.

stops.title: Render the expired message
stops.summary: The error case now has an early branch that prints a distinct "has expired" message, expiry lines and a tailored next step.
stops.purpose: This is the user-visible fix. It replaces the "invalid" wording and the interactive `gh auth refresh` hint.

necessity.reason: This is the output change the issue asks for.

points.text: When the flag is set, it prints the header and the active-account line.
points.why: so the entry still reads like other entries but says "has expired".

points.text: It writes the shared expiry lines.
points.why: so the reader sees why the check failed.

points.text: If the refresh token is also past expiry, it suggests `gh auth login`. Otherwise it suggests rerunning without the flag.
points.why: because a refresh can no longer succeed once the refresh token has expired.

points.text: A `break` skips the generic error output.
points.why: so the old "invalid" lines are not printed as well.

stops.check: Confirm `break` leaves the switch before the generic lines, so no "invalid" or `gh auth refresh` text appears.

stops.title: Share the expiry lines
stops.summary: The expiry printing is moved out of the success branch into a `writeExpiry` helper that both outputs call.
stops.purpose: The expired output must show the same lines as the healthy one. Without the helper, the code would be duplicated.

necessity.reason: It avoids duplicating the expiry printing; a small refactor tied directly to the feature.

points.text: The inline block in the success case is replaced by a helper call.
points.why: so the success output is unchanged.

points.text: The helper prints the expiring-token line, then token and refresh-token expiry with relative times.
points.why: so both outputs render identical text.

stops.check: Compare the helper body with the removed lines; the printed text should be identical.

stops.title: Tests for each branch
stops.summary: Four new cases cover the expired message, the refresh-also-expired variant, a 503, and a 401 on an unexpired token.
stops.purpose: They pin the exact output of the new branch. They also show the narrow trigger leaves other failures unchanged.

necessity.reason: They cover the new branch and its negative cases, but are not needed for the behaviour itself.

points.text: An expired token with a valid refresh token expects the "rerun without --no-refresh" hint.
points.why: to cover the main path from the issue.

points.text: An expired refresh token expects the `gh auth login` hint.
points.why: to cover the second variant in the description.

points.text: A 503 and an unexpired 401 expect the old "invalid" output.
points.why: to show the detection is limited to expired tokens that get a 401.

stops.check: Check that the negative cases fail without the 401 and expiry conditions in the detection.

checks.text: The detection depends on `entry.Refreshable` and `TokenExpiresAt` being set before the early return. The diff doesn't show this, so confirm it in `buildEntry`.
`errors.AsType` is a recent generic addition to the standard library. Confirm the module's Go version supports it and that `api.HTTPError` is matched by value, not pointer.
The hint wording is "run gh auth status (without --no-refresh)", not the issue's "without --no-refresh" phrasing. This is fine, but the exact text is now tested.
Expiry is compared to the local clock. A token the server rejected under a skewed clock could be mislabelled as expired, or an expired one not labelled; the 401 gate limits this.

questions: Does the other-accounts loop (inactive accounts) have a test with `--no-refresh`, or only the active account?

intent.summary: The diff implements the expected output from the issue, including the refresh-token-expired variant and keeping other failures unchanged.

items.requirement: Say the token has expired when `--no-refresh` hits an expired expiring token
items.evidence: A new branch prints "Token for … has expired" when the flag is set.
The expired branch calls the shared helper that prints expiry lines.

items.requirement: Hint at dropping `--no-refresh` to let gh refresh
items.evidence: The branch prints "To refresh it, run gh auth status (without --no-refresh)".

items.requirement: Suggest `gh auth login -h <host>` if the refresh token also expired
items.evidence: A branch checks whether the refresh token expiry is past and prints the login command.

items.requirement: Other failures such as revoked tokens keep the "invalid" wording
items.evidence: Detection requires a 401 and an expiry in the past; tests cover 503 and an unexpired 401.
